title: Equivariant coherent self-intersection along a regular immersion
statement:
For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $F$-scheme with a $G$-action and let $i:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be a $G$-equivariant closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ is regular near $W$: every point of $W$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $Y$ such that $\mathcal I(U)$ is generated by a regular sequence of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and these lengths are bounded independently of the point. Away from $W$ no condition is imposed. The conormal bundle is $N^\vee=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ on $W$, with its induced linearization. The finite alternating Tor formula
$$i^![\mathcal M]=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q[\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_Y}_q(\mathcal O_W,\mathcal M)]$$
defines an $R(G)$-linear homomorphism $G_0^G(Y)\to G_0^G(W)$; Tor is the homology of the derived tensor product, whose equivariance is the induced one. For every $\alpha\in G_0^G(W)$ one has
$$i^!i_*\alpha=\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)\alpha,\qquad \lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q[\bigwedge^q N^\vee],$$
where multiplication by this expression means the alternating sum of tensoring with its exterior-power bundles. If $\mathcal E$ is a $G$-linearized locally finite free module on $Y$, then $i^![\mathcal E]=[i^*\mathcal E]$. These identities hold in integer Grothendieck groups and include the empty immersion and codimension zero.

WANTED: Thomason, Une formule de Lefschetz en K-theorie equivariante algebrique (1986), self-intersection identity; not present locally. This is a local regular-immersion identity, not a fixed-point formula, and Milne does not prove it.

proof.text: The field $F$ is Noetherian, so finite type makes $Y$ Noetherian. The same holds for its closed subscheme $W$, affine-locally a quotient of a Noetherian ring. Write $\mathcal B=i_*\mathcal O_W=\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal I$ and fix the bound $c$ on the regular generators. Near $W$, every chosen regular tuple is Koszul-regular and its augmented Koszul complex is a finite free resolution of $\mathcal B$ of length at most $c$. Tensoring it with an arbitrary coherent $\mathcal M$ therefore computes Tor and gives zero in degrees $q>c$. Outside $W$ the first tensor factor is zero. The equivariant Tor calculus makes these coherent linearized $\mathcal B$-modules. Put $T_q(\mathcal M)=i^*T_q(\mathcal B,\mathcal M)$. Since $T_q(\mathcal B,\mathcal M)$ is quasi-coherent of finite type and killed by $\mathcal I$, the annihilated-pushforward lemma makes $T_q(\mathcal M)$ coherent ($W$ is Noetherian) with unit isomorphism $T_q(\mathcal B,\mathcal M)\cong i_*T_q(\mathcal M)$; exactness on $W$ is tested after $i_*$, which on stalks at points of $W$ is the identity. Linearization: put $j=\mathrm{id}_G\times i:G\times_FW\to G\times_FY$ and let $a_W$ be the restricted action; equivariance of $i$ gives $a\circ j=i\circ a_W$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2\circ j=i\circ\operatorname{pr}_{2,W}$. Pull the linearization $\psi$ of $T_q(\mathcal B,\mathcal M)$ back along $j$ and compose with the composition isomorphisms $(h\circ g)^*\cong g^*h^*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback]: this is an isomorphism $a_W^*T_q(\mathcal M)\cong\operatorname{pr}_{2,W}^*T_q(\mathcal M)$, and its identity and cocycle identities are the pullbacks of those of $\psi$ along $e\times i$ and $\mathrm{id}_G\times\mathrm{id}_G\times i$. Under the unit isomorphism, maps and exact sequences of linearized $\mathcal B$-modules on $Y$ correspond to those on $W$. The conormal bases furnished by the coefficient Tor lemma also show that $N^\vee$ and its exterior powers are locally finite free with ranks bounded by $c$.

proof.text: For an equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$, the Tor long exact sequence is a finite exact sequence of coherent linearized modules on $W$ by step 1. Write each term's class as the sum of the classes of the incoming image and the outgoing image. All image classes cancel in its alternating sum. With the order $T_c(\mathcal M'),T_c(\mathcal M),T_c(\mathcal M''),T_{c-1}(\mathcal M'),\ldots,T_0(\mathcal M'')$, the cancellation gives $\sum_q(-1)^q[T_q(\mathcal M)]=\sum_q(-1)^q[T_q(\mathcal M')]+\sum_q(-1)^q[T_q(\mathcal M'')]$. Thus the displayed formula respects the defining relations of $G_0^G(Y)$.

source.place: Tag 08BP, definition-tor and long exact sequence; equivariant tensor and Grothendieck relation assembly written by the agent.

proof.text: For a finite-dimensional rational $G$-module $V$, let $V_Y=\mathcal O_Y\otimes_FV$. The Tor tensor comparison identifies $T_q(\mathcal M\otimes V_Y)$ equivariantly with $T_q(\mathcal M)\otimes V_W$. Taking alternating classes gives $i^!([V]\,[\mathcal M])=[V]\,i^![\mathcal M]$. Tensor by $V_Y$ is exact, and a short exact sequence of representations remains exact after tensoring with any sheaf: over $F$ it is split as a sequence of vector spaces, which proves exactness on underlying modules, while the arrows retain their given equivariance. Consequently these actions respect the relations in $R(G)$ as well as those in $G_0^G$, and $i^!$ is $R(G)$-linear. For a linearized locally finite free $\mathcal E$, the same calculus gives only degree-zero Tor, namely $\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal E=i_*i^*\mathcal E$, proving $i^![\mathcal E]=[i^*\mathcal E]$.

source.place: Tag 08BP, definition-tor and long exact sequence; equivariant tensor and Grothendieck relation assembly written by the agent.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal N$ be a coherent linearized module on $W$. The closed immersion is finite, so its direct image is coherent, and $i_*$ is exact: on each ambient affine chart it is restriction of scalars from $A/I$ to $A$, which leaves the exact sequence of underlying abelian groups unchanged. Thus it induces the homomorphism $i_*$ in the question. On a regular chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, put $B=A/I$ and $M=\mathcal N(W\cap U)$. The coefficient Tor isomorphism gives $\operatorname{Tor}_q^A(B,M)\simeq\bigwedge_B^q(I/I^2)\otimes_BM$. These comparisons agree on overlaps: refine an overlap by affine opens, use the affine-restriction compatibility of Tor, and use the coefficient comparison's flat-base-change and regular-presentation independence. Hence they glue to sheaf isomorphisms $T_q(i_*\mathcal N)\simeq\bigwedge^qN^\vee\otimes\mathcal N$.

source.place: Tags 062F (lemma-regular-koszul-regular), 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular); agent assembly with equivariant Tor.

proof.text: These sheaf isomorphisms are equivariant. Indeed $\operatorname{pr}_2:G\times_FY\to Y$ is flat since $F[G]$ is a vector space over $F$. The automorphism $(g,y)\mapsto(g,gy)$ identifies the action map with that projection, so the action map is flat as well. Flat pullback carries $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ to the conormal of the pulled-back immersion. Pull the chart comparisons of step 4 back along the action and projection; the coefficient lemma identifies both pullbacks with the same normalized Tor comparison for the pulled-back ideal and pulled-back coefficients. Thus their square with the linearizations of $\mathcal N$ and the conormal commutes on an affine cover of $G\times_F W$, and therefore as sheaf maps. This uses no invariant affine chart, no equivariant regular generators, and no smoothness or reductivity of $G$.

source.place: Tag 0473, lemma-conormal-functorial-flat; equivariant gluing of the normalized coefficient Tor comparison written by the agent.

proof.text: Taking the finite alternating classes of the equivariant isomorphisms from steps 4--5 yields $i^!i_*[\mathcal N]=\sum_{q=0}^c(-1)^q[\bigwedge^qN^\vee\otimes\mathcal N]=\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)[\mathcal N]$. Tensoring with each exterior bundle is exact, so this equality extends through the relations to every $\alpha\in G_0^G(W)$. All cancellations take place over $\mathbf Z$. For $W=\varnothing$ all modules and both groups on $W$ are zero. For a length-zero regular chart the ideal is zero, the Koszul resolution has only degree zero, and $N^\vee=0$ with $\bigwedge^0N^\vee=\mathcal O_W$; thus the formula includes codimension zero and clopen immersions.
